answer: Each epoch an account must present a nullifier, a one-way tag derived from a scarce external credential and the epoch seed, so one credential yields exactly one valid tag and a repeat is rejected. A farm of n identities must buy n credentials, and because each purchase drains the same thin supply, the price per credential climbs with n instead of staying flat. Like a voyage across the delta of many gatekeepers where every hollow shortcut is sealed, the cheap path closes while a single honest agent pays once.
